# Q3 Sales Review

This is a synthetic sales-report example. The figures illustrate report structure and are not company results.

The example ends September at **$630K MRR**, up **61.5% from July's $390K**. Enterprise supplied $140K of the $240K increase; mid-market supplied the remaining $100K.

## What drove the lift

Enterprise MRR rose from $280K to $420K; mid-market rose from $110K to $210K. The rows establish those changes. They contain no customer, sales-cycle or intervention data, so they do not establish why the increases happened.

```chart
type: bar
title: MRR by segment, Q3
subtitle: Enterprise contributed 58.3% of the $240K increase from July to September
data:
  inline:
    - { month: Jul, mrr: 280000, segment: enterprise }
    - { month: Jul, mrr: 110000, segment: mid-market }
    - { month: Aug, mrr: 340000, segment: enterprise }
    - { month: Aug, mrr: 160000, segment: mid-market }
    - { month: Sep, mrr: 420000, segment: enterprise }
    - { month: Sep, mrr: 210000, segment: mid-market }
encoding:
  x: month
  y: mrr
  color: segment
axes:
  y: { label: MRR, format: number, unit: $ }
annotations:
  - { kind: point, at: { x: Aug, y: 340000 }, text: Enterprise reached $340K }
  - { kind: point, at: { x: Sep, y: 420000 }, text: Enterprise reached $420K }
style:
  ratio: "16:9"
```

## Forward look

```callout

body: |
  These synthetic monthly rows contain no pricing or retention evidence. Check real source data and distinguish recurring revenue from one-time effects before using a similar report for planning.
```

| Enterprise | $280K | $420K | +50% |
| Mid-market | $110K | $210K | +90.9% |
| Total | $390K | $630K | +61.5% |
